questions.stem: Which declaration creates an integer array of five elements?
questions.solution: int a[5]; reserves five integer elements.

questions.stem: Given the declaration, what is displayed?
questions.solution: word[3] is 't' because array indexing starts at zero.

questions.stem: Which identifier is valid in C++?
questions.solution: An identifier may contain letters, digits and underscores, but cannot start with a digit or be a keyword.

questions.stem: What is displayed by the following code?
questions.solution: x * 2 is 10; cout displays the value.

questions.stem: A computer system's hardware includes which of the following?
questions.solution: All five listed components are part of the hardware.

questions.stem: Which operator reads data from cin?
questions.solution: The extraction operator >> reads from an input stream.

questions.stem: Which of the following are selection structures?
questions.solution: if and switch select among alternatives.
% is the modulus operator and returns the remainder.

questions.stem: Which loop is guaranteed to execute its body at least once?
questions.solution: do...while tests the condition after the body.

questions.stem: Which structure chooses between two alternative paths?
This question tests high-level languages and debugging.

parts.text: Define syntax error and logic error.
parts.answer: A syntax error violates the language grammar and is detected by the compiler. A logic error produces incorrect output although the program runs.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Explain TWO advantages of high-level languages over machine language.
parts.answer: They are easier to read and write, portable across machines, and supported by compilers and debugging tools.
parts.solution: Award 1.5 marks for each valid advantage.
parts.label: b

questions.stem: A concert charges the ticket prices shown in Table 1. A negative age is invalid.

parts.text: Draw a flowchart for the ticket price selection.
parts.answer: Start -> read age -> if age < 0 display invalid; else if age <= 12 price = 15; else if age <= 17 price = 25; else price = 40 -> display price -> end.
parts.solution: Award marks for validation, all ranges, output and flow.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Write pseudocode and a complete C++ program for the ticket price selection.
parts.answer: Use if/else if with the three ranges and an invalid-age branch.
parts.solution: Award marks for validation, range conditions, assignment and output.
parts.label: b

questions.stem: This question tests declarations, constants and expressions.

parts.text: Write C++ declarations for: an integer age, a double price, a constant discount rate of 0.10 and a character grade.
parts.answer: int age; double price; const double DISCOUNT = 0.10; char grade;
parts.solution: Award marks for correct types, names and const initialisation.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Write C++ statements to read age and price, calculate price after discount, and display the result.
parts.answer: cin >> age >> price; price = price - price * DISCOUNT; cout << price;
parts.solution: Award marks for input, discount expression and output.
parts.label: b

questions.stem: Study the following array program segment:

parts.text: Trace the program and state the output.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Rewrite the segment using a do...while loop that sums only values greater than 5.
parts.answer: int i=0,s=0; do { if(a[i]>5) s+=a[i]; i++; } while(i<5); cout<<s;
parts.solution: Award marks for do...while, condition, filter and output.
parts.label: b

questions.stem: A sports club records the sport names and medal counts in Table 1.

parts.text: Declare two parallel arrays for the five sports in Table 1 and initialise them with those values.
parts.solution: Award marks for both declarations, correct sizes and related indices.
parts.label: a

parts.text: Write a program segment to display each sport with its medals, then calculate the total and average medals.
parts.answer: Loop i=0..4 to display sports[i] and medals[i], accumulate total, average = double(total)/5.
parts.solution: Award marks for paired display, total, average and output.
parts.label: b

parts.solution: Award 3 marks for input, 4 for total/average, 3 for highest/index, 3 for above-average count and 2 for output.

questions.stem: A cafe sells the items shown in Table 1. A 10% discount is given when the subtotal is at least RM50.
questions.solution: Award 3 marks for input, 5 for price/subtotal, 4 for discount, 2 for formatting and 1 for completeness.

parts.text: Write a complete C++ program that reads the item code and quantity, calculates the subtotal and discount, and displays a formatted receipt with the item name, quantity, subtotal, discount and amount to pay.
parts.solution: Award 3 marks for input, 5 for price/subtotal, 4 for discount, 2 for formatting and 1 for completeness.
